title: MCP Static Scanner Validation Survey
subtitle: Human Evaluation of MCP Tool and Resource Risk
intro:
This study evaluates a static risk-scanning approach for Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools — the layer that lets an AI agent use services such as Google Calendar, GitHub and Slack.

You will rate the MCP servers below with respect to three MCP security aspects: Tool Impact, Asset Sensitivity and Blast Radius. Each section says what to ignore, so please keep them apart and judge only from the information given.
consent: I understand the purpose of the study and agree that my anonymized responses may be used for research and evaluation of the proposed risk-scoring method.

impact.label: Liveness
impact.meaning: The system only says “I am here.” Nothing about the data is touched or revealed (ping, health, version, whoami).

impact.label: Metadata
impact.meaning: The shape of the data, never its substance: names, ids, counts, sizes, timestamps, permissions, a listing — or a change to labels and read/unread state only.

impact.label: Read content
impact.meaning: The substance is disclosed and nothing changes: actual bodies and values are returned (read, get, fetch, export). Afterwards the system is exactly as before.

impact.label: Recoverable write
impact.meaning: State changes and the system can undo it: something is created, edited in part, moved, or posted where it can still be deleted. Permission and membership changes belong here too.

impact.label: Irreversible
impact.meaning: No path back from inside the system: content destroyed or fully overwritten, code executed, money moved, or a message sent outside (email, webhook, public post) where it cannot be recalled.

sensitivity.label: Public
sensitivity.meaning: Already published or disposable. Nothing left to lose but uptime.

sensitivity.label: Routine
sensitivity.meaning: Low-value internal material — onboarding guides, templates, org charts. Barely worth stealing.

sensitivity.label: Internal
sensitivity.meaning: Meant to stay in-house. A leak is awkward and briefly useful to others, but not lasting damage — project docs, schemas, ordinary team schedules.

sensitivity.label: Restricted
sensitivity.meaning: A leak causes serious, lasting harm to customers, staff or the organization, but is not instantly usable the way a live credential is — customer and production data, payroll and HR, proprietary source, audit logs.

sensitivity.label: Critical
sensitivity.meaning: Exposure alone is an emergency: exploitable or legally reportable the moment it leaks — live credentials and keys, regulated records such as patient or card data, money-moving material.

blast.label: Negligible
blast.meaning: One item among many, one person at most. The asset as a whole is untouched.

blast.label: Minor
blast.meaning: A few items or one small bounded scope. Real but local, and easy to restore.

blast.label: Major
blast.meaning: Most of the asset, or several whole scopes in one call. Serious, but still partial.

blast.label: Total but contained
blast.meaning: Essentially everything the asset holds — but the consequences stop at its boundary. Full coverage of an ordinary asset is 4, never 5.

blast.label: Systemic
blast.meaning: The consequences escape the asset. Award 5 only through one of the three routes listed below.

step_prompts.impact: Rate the tool impact of MCP tools. Think about what the tool may perform. A short description of every tool is given beneath its name. Judge each tool on its own, not against the others.
step_prompts.sensitivity: Rate the asset itself, whichever tool reaches it. A short description of every asset is given beneath its name. Judge each asset on its own, not against the others. Levels may repeat. Rate what the asset normally holds, not the worst it could ever hold.
step_prompts.blast: Rate the potential effect of a tool on an asset at scale. Think about “How far does one call reach?” Score every tool and asset pair from 1 to 5. Where a tool barely touches an asset, that is a 1 — the lowest rung of the scale, not a skipped cell.

servers.title: Google Calendar
servers.scenario: CBG's workplace-services team runs the agent against the real 13-tool Google Calendar surface. The central fact for this organization is that event metadata is itself sensitive: attendee lists and titles disclose unannounced deals, candidates and departures without anyone opening an event body. Knowing which calendars exist is not — the container list is routine.

tools.name: get-current-time
tools.desc: Returns the current time in a given time zone. Reaches no calendar and no event.

tools.name: list-calendars
tools.desc: Returns the calendars the account can see — names, ids and basic attributes. No events.

tools.name: get-freebusy
tools.desc: Returns busy and free blocks for the calendars named. No titles, no attendees.

tools.name: get-event
tools.desc: Returns one event in full: title, description, location and the attendee list.

tools.name: search-events
tools.desc: Returns the events matching a query, with their titles and attendees.

tools.name: create-event
tools.desc: Creates a new event, optionally inviting attendees by email.

tools.name: delete-event
tools.desc: Permanently removes an existing event from the calendar.

servers.title: GitHub
servers.scenario: CBG's engineering organization runs the agent against the vendor's 26-tool GitHub catalog. CBG does not disclose its repository inventory to integrators: the list of private repository names alone maps the product estate and the production topology. The assets below therefore name classes of repository and the mutable states this surface can reach, not the repositories themselves.

tools.name: list_commits
tools.desc: Returns commit messages and metadata for a repository. No file contents.

tools.name: list_issues
tools.desc: Returns issue titles and metadata. No issue bodies.

tools.name: get_file_contents
tools.desc: Returns the contents of one file, named by exact path.

tools.name: search_code
tools.desc: Returns matching lines of code from across the repositories in scope.

tools.name: create_or_update_file
tools.desc: Writes one file, creating it or replacing its contents.

tools.name: create_pull_request
tools.desc: Opens a proposed change for review. Nothing is merged yet.

tools.name: merge_pull_request
tools.desc: Merges an approved pull request into its target branch.

assets.name: public-website
assets.desc: The public marketing site repository; already published

assets.name: repository-catalog
assets.desc: The list of repository names, descriptions and visibility; no code

assets.desc: Internal engineering documentation and runbooks

assets.name: ml-research

assets.name: repository-contents
assets.desc: What a file read or write reaches: code bodies across every repo in scope

assets.name: infra-config
assets.desc: Terraform and deploy configuration for the production estate; a merge reconfigures production

assets.name: infra-config

assets.name: payments-service

assets.desc: Core service source; a merge reaches production behavior

assets.name: ml-research
assets.desc: Unpublished research, models and dataset pointers

assets.name: issues-and-comments
assets.desc: Issue threads and their comments; internal discussion

servers.title: Slack
servers.scenario: CBG's Slack workspace runs on the real 16-tool API surface. CBG does not publish a channel inventory or classification list to integrators: private channel names themselves reveal organizational structure — who is in an incident, what HR is discussing. Note what this surface includes beyond messaging: user-group administration and channel join/leave are access-control operations wearing messaging clothes.

tools.name: channels_list
tools.desc: Returns the channels in the workspace — names and topics. No messages.

tools.name: conversations_unreads
tools.desc: Returns unread counts and read markers across conversations. No message bodies.

tools.name: conversations_history
tools.desc: Returns the recent messages in one channel.

tools.name: conversations_search_messages
tools.desc: Returns matching messages from across the workspace.

tools.name: conversations_add_message
tools.desc: Posts a message into a channel.

tools.name: usergroups_create
tools.desc: Creates a new user group.

tools.name: usergroups_users_update
tools.desc: Replaces the membership of a user group — the access list for private channels.

assets.name: announcements
assets.desc: Broadcast channel, already seen by everyone; only spoofing matters

assets.name: channel-directory
assets.desc: The list of channels, their names and topics; no messages

assets.name: engineering
assets.desc: Ordinary engineering traffic

assets.name: hr-internal
assets.desc: HR private channel — personnel matters and salary data

assets.name: incident-response

servers.title: Filesystem
servers.scenario: CBG's corporate file share is served to the agent through the real 14-tool filesystem server. Engineering material, payroll, security key material and product source sit in one tree, and CBG does not publish the file listing: the layout maps which teams hold what, and the security scope's very existence is a target. Classify by data type, not by where a path happens to sit.

tools.name: list_allowed_directories
tools.desc: Returns the roots this server is permitted to serve. No file names, no contents.

tools.name: list_directory
tools.desc: Lists the entries of one directory, files and directories distinguished. No contents.

tools.name: directory_tree
tools.desc: Returns the whole recursive tree of names and paths beneath a directory. No contents.

tools.name: read_file
tools.desc: Returns the complete text of one file, named by exact path.

tools.name: read_multiple_files
tools.desc: Returns the complete contents of several named files in one call.

tools.name: edit_file
tools.desc: Replaces exact line sequences inside an existing file and leaves the rest untouched.

tools.name: write_file
tools.desc: Creates a file, or completely overwrites an existing one with new content.

servers.title: SQL Database
servers.scenario: CBG's research-operations database is a single SQLite store on a 5-tool server, holding the project register, experiment records, dataset provenance, staff records and the API credentials the research pipeline uses to reach other services. CBG does not publish the schema to integrators: the table names alone map which systems we integrate with and where the credentials live. Classify by what a table characteristically holds.

tools.name: list_tables
tools.desc: Returns the names of every table in the database. No columns, no rows.

tools.name: describe_table
tools.desc: Returns the column names and types of one named table. No cell values.

tools.name: read_query
tools.desc: Returns the rows matching a read-only SELECT the caller writes, up to 100. Nothing changes.

tools.name: insert_row
tools.desc: Inserts one new row into a named table.

tools.name: write_query
tools.desc: Runs an INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE the caller writes. DDL is blocked; there is no rollback.

assets.name: publications
assets.desc: Published papers and citations; only unreleased pre-print status is sensitive

assets.name: table-metadata
assets.desc: Column names and types for one table; schema only

assets.name: projects
assets.desc: The internal project register

assets.name: datasets
assets.desc: Pre-publication research data and its provenance

assets.name: employees
assets.desc: Staff records: salary, contact details, one row per person

assets.name: api_keys
assets.desc: Stored service credentials — one row is independently usable against another system

assets.name: api_keys
assets.desc: Stored service credentials — one row is independently usable against another system

assets.name: employees
assets.desc: Staff records: salary, contact details, one row per person

assets.name: grants
assets.desc: Funding terms and award amounts; a tampered row misstates a sponsor commitment

assets.name: database-records
assets.desc: What an unrestricted query returns: the caller names the table, so this reaches whatever the credential can see

assets.name: table-catalog
assets.desc: The list of table names. No cell values, but the names map the integrations
